source: Domiciano de Souza et al. (2014), The environment of the fast rotating star Achernar. III. Photospheric parameters revealed by the VLTI, A&A 569, A10 (https://doi.org/10.1051/0004-6361/201424144), Table 6, read from the open copy at https://hal.science/hal-02548378
caption: Physical parameters of Achernar derived from the fit of the RVZ model (CHARRON code) to VLTI/PIONIER H band data using the MCMC method (emcee code). The fit adopts a mass of 6.1 solar masses, a mean effective temperature of 15 000 K and a distance of 42.75 pc.

omega.cell: Critical rotation rate: Veq/Vc; Ω/Ωc 0.883; 0.980 (a derived parameter, printed without an uncertainty; ω is Ω/Ωc)

poleTemperatureK.cell: Polar temperature: Tp (K) 17 124 (derived, no uncertainty printed)

equatorTemperatureK.cell: Equatorial temperature: Teq (K) 12 673 (derived, no uncertainty printed)

polarRadiusSolar.cell: Polar radius: Rp (R⊙) 6.78 (derived, no uncertainty printed)

polePositionAngleDegrees.cell: Position angle of the visible pole: PArot (°) 216.9 (+0.4; −0.4)

note: The table names the position angle as the visible pole's, so that pole is the one tilted toward us. The same table derives Req/Rp 1.352, a rotation period of 37.25 h and an equatorial velocity of 298.8 km/s. The fit's mean temperature is an adopted 15 000 K, not a fitted one; only the pole-to-equator contrast of the model is drawn, around the star's measured disc color.
